title: Moneyview Shares End Market Debut 59% Above Issue Price
excerpt: The digital lender listed at Rs 55.6 on the BSE — a 64% premium to its Rs 34 IPO price — and closed its maiden session at Rs 54.03 with a Rs 9,510 crore market cap.
body:
• Moneyview closed its maiden trading session at Rs 54.03 on the BSE, 58.9% above its Rs 34 issue price, after listing at Rs 55.6 — a 64% premium — and touching an intraday high of Rs 62.
  • The Rs 1,092 crore IPO was subscribed about 98 times, with institutional investors bidding more than 227 times their allotted quota; anchor investors included SBI Mutual Fund and Goldman Sachs.
  • Valued at Rs 5,985 crore at issue, the digital lender ended the day at roughly Rs 9,510 crore, making it one of the strongest fintech debuts of the year.
  • The listing was backed by operating numbers: Q1 FY27 net profit jumped 2.6 times to Rs 173.8 crore, while operating revenue rose 50.2% to Rs 1,041.1 crore.

Digital lender Moneyview ended its market debut about 59% above its issue price, capping one of the strongest fintech listings of the year. The stock, which listed at Rs 55.6 on the BSE — a 64% premium to the Rs 34 IPO price — touched an intraday high of Rs 62 before settling at Rs 54.03, according to Inc42. On the NSE it listed at Rs 55 and closed around Rs 53.4, up roughly 57-59% from issue price.

A blockbuster listing day

The listing beat grey-market expectations, which had pegged the debut around Rs 48.60. Moneyview's market capitalisation stood at Rs 9,788.6 crore (about $1.01 billion) at listing and ended the session at about Rs 9,510.5 crore (roughly $988 million) — up sharply from the Rs 5,985 crore valuation at the IPO price. Demand for the Rs 1,092 crore issue had been overwhelming from the start: it was fully subscribed within hours on the first day of bidding and closed at about 98 times overall subscription, with qualified institutional buyers oversubscribing their quota by 227.45 times. The issue was anchored by investors including SBI Mutual Fund and Goldman Sachs, which were allotted 9.63 crore equity shares for a total investment of Rs 327.5 crore. The IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 750 crore and an offer for sale of up to 10.05 crore shares worth around Rs 341.7 crore, priced at the top of the Rs 32-34 band.

"Moneyview's journey from a financial data-focused idea to a scaled consumer platform focused on credit for Bharat has been remarkable."

— Subrata Mitra, Founding Partner, Accel

Context & background

Founded in 2014 by IIT Delhi graduates Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview began as a digital-only, credit-led fintech offering unsecured personal loans to underserved and new-to-credit borrowers. It partners with banks and NBFCs to offer loans through its app and website, and also lends in-house through its NBFC arm, Whizdm Finance. Beyond its flagship personal loan business launched in 2017, the company has expanded into earned wage access, home loans, loans against property, digital gold and UPI transactions. Of the fresh issue proceeds, Rs 325 crore will support loan disbursals under default loss guarantee arrangements, while Rs 250 crore goes into augmenting the capital base of its NBFC subsidiary.

Impact & analysis

The debut was backed by operating momentum rather than hype alone. Moneyview's consolidated net profit jumped 2.6 times to Rs 173.8 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 67.2 crore a year earlier, while operating revenue rose 50.2% to Rs 1,041.1 crore from Rs 693 crore. For FY26, operating revenue grew to Rs 3,351.2 crore from Rs 2,339.1 crore, and consolidated profit edged up to Rs 242.7 crore. The muted profit growth for the full year — barely above FY25's Rs 240.3 crore — is worth watching against the listing pop: the market is paying for the growth trajectory, and future quarters will need to show profit scaling with revenue. Same-day debutant A-One Steels India, by contrast, listed at a modest 12-14% premium and ended barely 3% up, underscoring how unusual Moneyview's reception was.

Diaspora angle

For diaspora investors, Moneyview's debut is another data point in India's 2026 IPO boom — the kind of domestic-demand story that has made Indian fintech one of the most watched emerging-market plays. The listing also underlines the depth of India's digital-lending market, a sector many NRI investors access through India-focused mutual funds and fintech ETFs.

What's next

Watch how the stock trades in its first month — debut pops often fade once anchor lock-ins and profit-booking set in. The bigger signal is whether the IPO pipeline holds: a strong Moneyview listing encourages other Indian fintechs sitting on the sidelines. Q2 FY27 results will test whether the profit momentum of the June quarter is sustainable.
